hypothesis.title: payment flagd config enabled paymentFailure flag to 25%, causing token validation errors
hypothesis.summary: The flagd-config ConfigMap was changed 10 minutes before the alert, setting the paymentFailure feature flag from 'off' to '25%'. This caused payment to reject ~25% of requests with "Invalid token" errors for gold loyalty customers. These errors propagated upstream to checkout, triggering the CheckoutHighErrorRate alert. Payment's own metrics show a matching 24.8% error rate with no resource or latency issues.
hypothesis.reasoning: The alert fired for checkout's high error rate (23%), but the telemetry clearly shows checkout is a victim, not the root cause. 98% of failing checkout traces end in payment (evidence traces:checkout:summary shows 42/43 errors originate in payment). The error logs from both services show the same message: "Payment request failed. Invalid token. app.loyalty.level=gold" (logs:payment:1, logs:checkout:1). Payment's own error rate spiked from 0.4% to 24.8% at the same time (metrics:payment:error_rate). The timing is critical: the configmap/flagd-config changed the paymentFailure flag from 'off' to '25%' 10 minutes before the alert (changes:payment:config:0), and error logs first appeared 9 minutes before the alert. Payment's CPU, memory, and latency metrics are all healthy, ruling out resource saturation. The ad deployment 26 minutes before the alert is a red herring—ad is not on the failing call path from checkout to payment. The fraud-detection restart (exit 137, likely OOMKilled) is also unrelated since fraud-detection is an async Kafka consumer, not in the synchronous checkout flow. This matches the pattern in RB-flagd and similar config-driven failures. The root cause is the feature-flag config change enabling synthetic payment failures.

supporting_evidence.why_it_matters: ConfigMap flagd-config changed paymentFailure from 'off' to '25%' exactly 10 minutes before the alert, matching the timing of the error spike.
418 ERROR logs in payment with 'Invalid token' message first appeared 9 minutes before alert, immediately after the config change.
Payment error rate jumped from 0.4% to 24.8% (close to the 25% flag value), confirming the flag is actively causing failures.
98% (42/43) of failing checkout traces terminate in payment, proving payment is the error origin, not checkout.
Example trace shows the error originates in payment:payment/handle span with the exact 'Invalid token' message, then propagates to checkout.
Payment latency remains stable at ~46ms, ruling out resource saturation or datastore issues as the cause.

suggested_actions.title: Revert the paymentFailure feature flag to 'off' in flagd-config
suggested_actions.command: kubectl -n otel-demo get cm flagd-config -o yaml | sed 's/"paymentFailure": "25%"/"paymentFailure": "off"/' | kubectl apply -f -
suggested_actions.rationale: The paymentFailure flag was changed from 'off' to '25%' 10 minutes before the alert and is directly causing 25% of payment requests to fail. Reverting it will immediately stop the synthetic failures.

suggested_actions.title: Verify error rate drops after flag revert
suggested_actions.command: kubectl -n otel-demo logs -l app=payment --tail=50 --timestamps | grep -i error
suggested_actions.rationale: Confirm that payment error logs stop appearing after the flag is reverted, validating the mitigation.

suggested_actions.title: Check flagd-config change history and notify the team
suggested_actions.command: kubectl -n otel-demo get cm flagd-config -o jsonpath='{.data.demo\.flagd\.json}' | jq .
suggested_actions.rationale: Identify who made the config change and whether it was intentional (e.g., chaos testing) or accidental, to prevent recurrence.

alternatives.why_less_likely: Checkout was deployed 37 minutes before the alert (changes:checkout:deploy:2), but errors only started 9 minutes before the alert, 28 minutes after the deploy. The timing doesn't match, and traces show errors originate in payment, not checkout.

Ad was deployed 26 minutes before the alert, but ad is not on the call path from checkout to payment. The failing traces show no ad involvement, and the error message is payment-specific ('Invalid token').
